2027-06-30.title: Wednesday of the Thirteenth Week in Ordinary Time · The First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church
readings: God has heard the voice of the boy where he is
The Lord hears the cry of the poor
When they saw him, they begged him to leave their neighborhood
2027-06-30.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 13 (Year I). The optional memorial of the First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church may be kept: the Christians put to death in Rome under the emperor Nero, remembered on the day after the apostles Peter and Paul. Psalm verses are given in NRSV numbering. Liturgical colour: green (red if the memorial is kept).
2027-06-30.verse: And God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
theo: The promise is fulfilled at last: “Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.” Sarah's laugh of doubt has become a laugh of joy. But today's reading does not let us rest in the happy ending. At the feast for Isaac's weaning Sarah sees Ishmael, the son of the Egyptian slave woman Hagar, “playing with her son Isaac,” and she demands: “Cast out this slave woman with her son.” Scripture does not hide the hurt in this family. “The matter was very distressing to Abraham on account of his son,” for Ishmael too is his child. God tells Abraham to let them go, because the covenant line will pass through Isaac, but adds a promise for the other son: “As for the son of the slave woman, I will make a nation of him also, because he is your offspring.” Early in the morning Abraham gives Hagar bread and a skin of water and sends her away with the child. The scene in the wilderness of Beer-sheba is one of the most heartbreaking in the Bible. The water runs out. Hagar puts the boy under a bush and sits down “about the distance of a bowshot,” because she cannot bear to watch him die, and she weeps aloud. And then: “God heard the voice of the boy.” The name Ishmael means “God hears.” The angel calls from heaven: “What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid.” Then “God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water.” The well was there all along; she could not see it through her tears. “God was with the boy, and he grew up.” This is the second time Hagar has met God in the desert (Genesis 16), and she is the only person in the Old Testament who gives God a name: “You are El-roi,” the God who sees (Genesis 16:13). The God of Abraham is not the God of one family only; he hears the cry of the outcast, the foreign slave woman, the thirsty child. Jewish, Christian and Muslim traditions all remember Hagar and Ishmael. The Psalm sings the same truth: “This poor soul cried, and was heard by the LORD, and was saved from every trouble.”

In the Gospel Jesus crosses the lake to “the country of the Gadarenes,” Gentile territory east of the Sea of Galilee, where pigs were kept. Two men possessed by demons come out of the tombs to meet him, so violent that “no one could pass that way.” They live among the dead, cut off from every human community. The demons recognise Jesus at once and cry out: “What have you to do with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?” They know that their time is short, that the Son of God has come to destroy their power. They beg to be sent into a herd of swine, and Jesus says one word: “Go!” The whole herd rushes down the steep bank into the sea and perishes. The two men are set at liberty. But the ending is sad and surprising: “the whole town came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their neighborhood.” They had lost their pigs; they did not want to lose anything more. Two human beings had been restored, but the town counted its losses. It is possible to prefer our comfort, our business and our habits to the Lord who sets people at liberty. Hagar's eyes were opened and she saw the well; the Gadarenes saw the Lord and asked him to go. Today the Church also remembers the first martyrs of the Church of Rome, the many Christians whom Nero blamed for the great fire of the city in the year 64. The Roman historian Tacitus records that they were mocked, torn by dogs, crucified, and burned as torches in the night. Some were probably among those to whom St Paul had written his Letter to the Romans. Their names are known to God alone. Unlike the Gadarenes, they did not ask Jesus to leave; they let everything go rather than lose him.
outline: Ask: have you ever been unable to see the help God had already placed in front of you, because of your tears?
Hagar and Ishmael cast out into the desert, and the God who hears the voice of the boy.
The well was already there; God gives sight to see his help.
Point 3 · Do not send him away
The Gadarenes ask Jesus to leave; the first martyrs of Rome would not let him go.
“God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.”
live: Notice today one person who is pushed aside, a domestic worker, a migrant, a child in a difficult home, and do something concrete for them.
Ask yourself what you are afraid to lose if Jesus enters a part of your life, your money, a habit, a relationship, and let him in.
2027-06-30.prayer: God of Abraham, you heard the voice of the boy Ishmael and opened Hagar's eyes to see the well. Hear the cry of the poor, the outcast and the thirsty in our land, and open our eyes to the help you have already placed before us. Lord Jesus, you crossed the sea to release captives, and some asked you to leave; never let us prefer our possessions to you. Through the prayers of the first martyrs of the Church of Rome, who gave up everything rather than lose you, make us faithful to the end. Amen.
altar: At every Mass we share the water of life that Hagar could not see: Christ himself, who gives himself as food and drink. The first martyrs of Rome received the Eucharist in homes and catacombs, and from it drew the strength to die for him. Before the Gospel, when we sign our forehead, lips and heart, we ask that the Word may open our eyes, as God opened Hagar's.

quick: Sarah asks Abraham to send away Hagar and Ishmael; in the desert, when the water runs out, God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to see a well.
God promises to make Ishmael too a great nation, for he is Abraham's son.
Jesus delivers two possessed men in the land of the Gadarenes, but the town begs him to leave.
2027-06-30.action: Do one concrete good thing today for someone who is pushed aside.
2027-06-30.question: Is there a part of my life where I am asking Jesus to leave because I am afraid of what it will cost?
kidsaint: Not long after Jesus rose from the dead, there were many Christians in the big city of Rome. In the year 64 a terrible fire burned much of the city, and the cruel emperor Nero blamed the Christians. Many of them, men, women and young people, were killed because they would not stop believing in Jesus. We do not know their names, but God knows every one of them. Lesson: even if nobody knows your name, God sees your faithfulness and loves you.

family.explain: Hagar and her little boy Ishmael were sent away into the desert. When their water was finished, Hagar was so sad that she sat down and cried. But God heard the voice of the boy! An angel said: do not be afraid. Then God opened Hagar's eyes and she saw a well of water. God hears children when they cry, and he cares for people whom others push away.
family.intention: We pray for children who are thirsty, hungry or abandoned, and for mothers who struggle alone.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone our family can help this week, someone who feels left out or alone?”

illus: A social worker in Kochi tells of a young mother from a northern state who was left without money or papers when the contractor her husband worked for disappeared. For two days she sat with her small son outside the railway station, too frightened and ashamed to ask anyone for help. On the third morning a parish volunteer who sold tea nearby noticed the boy crying and asked what was wrong. Within a day the parish's migrant help desk had found them food, shelter and a way home. The mother said later: the help was in the same street all along; I could not see it until someone heard my son. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God who sees and hears, open our eyes to see your help and our ears to hear the cry of the poor. Amen.
share: God heard the voice of the boy (Genesis 21:17). Whose cry around me am I being asked to hear today?
God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water (Genesis 21:19). Where has God's help been near me while I could see only my troubles?
They begged him to leave their neighborhood (Matthew 8:34). What am I afraid to lose if I let Jesus fully into my life?
pm.resp: The Lord hears the cry of the poor.
interc: For the Church, that she may always hear the cry of the outcast and the stranger, as God heard Hagar and Ishmael.
For migrant workers and their families in Kerala and across India, especially those without help or papers.
For all who are possessed by addiction, violence or despair, that Christ may deliver them.
For Christians persecuted today, through the prayers of the first martyrs of Rome.
For our group, that we may never prefer our comfort or possessions to the Lord.
pm.close: Father, you hear the poor and release captives in your Son. Open our eyes to see your gifts and keep us faithful to Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today's first reading is a hard story. At last Isaac is born, the son of the promise. But in the same house there is another boy, Ishmael, the son of the slave woman Hagar. Sarah wants them sent away. Abraham is deeply distressed, because Ishmael is his son too. And early in the morning Hagar and her boy are sent into the desert with a little bread and a skin of water.

The water runs out. Hagar lays the child under a bush, goes a bowshot away and weeps, because she cannot watch him die. And then the Bible says: God heard the voice of the boy (Genesis 21:17). Do not be afraid. God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. The well was there all the time. She could not see it through her tears. How often that happens to us. We are so full of fear that we do not see the help God has already placed beside us.

And notice whom God hears: not the important people at the feast, but a foreign slave woman and a crying child in the desert. Ishmael's name means God hears. Our God is the God who hears the poor. If we want to be his people, we must hear them too: the migrant worker, the abandoned mother, the child who cries at night.

In the Gospel Jesus delivers two men who lived among the tombs. A whole herd of pigs is lost. And the people of the town come out and beg Jesus to leave. They preferred their pigs to their neighbours' deliverance, and their business to the Son of God. Today we also remember the first martyrs of Rome, who were burned and crucified under Nero. They did the opposite of the Gadarenes: they lost everything rather than lose Jesus. Let us ask for their courage, and let us never ask the Lord to leave. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother named Hagar and her little boy Ishmael were walking in the hot desert. Their water was finished, and the boy was crying. His mother was crying too. But God heard the boy! An angel said: do not be afraid. God opened Hagar's eyes and she saw a well full of water! God always hears children when they cry. So when you are sad or afraid, talk to God. He is listening.

intro: Theme: “God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.”
The God who hears the outcast and opens our eyes, and the Lord whom some send away and the martyrs would not let go.

q: And God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
points.apply: Tell God honestly this week the fear you have been carrying alone, and let someone you trust help you carry it.

sub: God with the boy as he grew.
q: Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. She went, and filled the skin with water, and gave the boy a drink.
but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.
points.apply: Each night this week name one help God gave you that day which you did not notice at first.

sub: The martyrs who would not let him go.
q: This poor soul cried, and was heard by the Lord, and was saved from every trouble.
Then the whole town came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their neighborhood.
points.apply: Give Jesus this week the one area of your life you have been keeping closed to him.

concl: God hears the cry of the outcast and opens Hagar's eyes to the well that was already there.
Some ask Jesus to leave because they fear their losses; the first martyrs of Rome lost everything rather than lose him.
2027-06-30.resolve: This week listen for one cry you have been ignoring, and answer it in Jesus' name.
